detections.evidence_quote: They were either drowned in the lake itself, or they were tossed in the lake after they were already murdered.
detections.summary: Legend relays that Native Americans were killed by settlers, drowned in the lake or thrown in after being murdered.

detections.evidence_quote: a ton of people have been murdered there
detections.summary: Some believe the road's name comes from the many people murdered there.

detections.evidence_quote: They'd slit your throat if you were traveling by, and steal everything that you were traveling with.
detections.summary: Highway robbers would ambush travellers on the shady stretch and slit their throats.

detections.evidence_quote: they hung them from all those low hanging trees
detections.summary: Locals are said to have hanged the robbers from the trees and left the bodies up as a warning.

detections.evidence_quote: another possible reason for the name of the road is actually a rather deadly malaria outbreak back in 1850.
detections.summary: A deadly 1850 malaria outbreak spread by mosquitoes from local swampland, described by a doctor of the time, ended when New Jersey drained the swamp in 1884.

detections.evidence_quote: Three confirmed murders have taken place in the area.
detections.summary: Three confirmed murders in the area in the 1920s-30s: a man killed with a car jack, a husband decapitated by his wife, and a man shot to death in a still-cold case.
